review.translation: [And let them be|0] [as lights|1] [in the expanse of|2] [the heavens|3] [to give light|4] [on|5] [the earth|6].” [And it was|7] [so|8].

analysis.evidence: The plural subject is the lights named in the preceding verse. לִמְאוֹרֹת gives their role, “as lights,” and לְהָאִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ states their purpose, “to give light on the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Qal weqatal, third person common plural, with prefixed וְ. It continues the directive of the preceding verse.

analysis.evidence: With וְהָיוּ, the prefixed לִ־ marks the role the lights are to serve. The phrase לְהָאִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ gives their purpose, to give light upon the earth.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לִ־ prefixed to a masculine plural absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם means ‘in the expanse of the heavens’. The construct noun takes הַשָּׁמַיִם as its complement, and the prepositional phrase locates the lights that illuminate the earth.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בִּ־ ‘in’ + masculine singular construct noun.

analysis.evidence: In בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם, “in the expanse of the sky,” הַשָּׁמַיִם completes the construct phrase. The lights shine from that expanse onto the earth below.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + masculine plural common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: לְהָאִיר states the purpose of the luminaries in the expanse of the heavens. עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where they give light: upon the earth.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed לְ expressing purpose

analysis.evidence: In לְהָאִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ, “to shine upon the earth,” עַל introduces the surface on which the light falls.
The lights are set בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם ‘in the expanse of the heavens’ to shine עַל הָאָרֶץ ‘upon the earth’. The earth is the whole realm below that receives their light.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי כֵן, כֵן (“so”) refers back to the command for the lights to shine on the earth. The phrase reports its fulfillment: “and it was so.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed narrative וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי כֵן (“and it was so”), כֵן refers back to the command that the lights shine on the earth. It indicates that what God commanded came to pass.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of manner with no prefix or suffix.
